title: Rational equality comparison unification: rejected runtime candidate, retained oracle and benchmarks

decision.runtime: Rejected all three equality-to-PartialOrd delegation variants; production comparison.rs remains byte-identical to the baseline.
decision.reason: The final guarded variant improves separated-wide and common equality cases, but costs 17.13% on close-wide equality, 3.94% on selected-fiber replay, 6.96% on the seven-pair cold conic/cubic lane, and 4.67% on matrix inverse. These representative regressions outweigh the runtime's 15-line reduction under the requested priority order.
decision.retained: One independent 110-value/12,100-ordered-pair cross-product oracle (two replay passes) and eight Criterion equality cases. The dispatch assertion requiring the rejected optimization is not retained.

sources.archived_state: The seven-repository snapshot is restored to the final evaluated guarded candidate and its original evaluation workloads after the retained baseline-runtime qualification. Root retained-* files record the actually committed test/benchmark additions.
sources.concurrent_drafts: Nine modified Computable files and one untracked fractional-separation test file in live Hyperreal were excluded and left untouched.

regressions.oracle: The independent cross-product test passes original and all candidates across canonical/unreduced values, zero, both signs, common denominators, dyadics, and 129/257/521/1025/4097-bit families.
regressions.experimental_dispatch: The non-retained trace test fails original production and passes all candidates. It verifies existing leading-interval decisions and the exact fallback for close unequal and scaled-unreduced equal values.
regressions.fairness: Scalar benchmark bodies and 729-test experimental catalogs match across all four revisions; geometry test bodies and 916-test catalogs match across both. Baseline and candidates build in the same archived paths. Only the final retained benchmark description changes; timing bodies remain identical.

retained_validation.runtime: Unchanged pinned production; no new ecosystem runtime claim.

validation.reason: First compile failed on a read-only ccache in the sandbox; approved escalated retry succeeded.

scope: Seven commit-pinned archives without live dependency symlinks; only the three scoped Hyperreal files are changed.
Hyperreal default uses --all-targets; all-feature suites include ignored tests.
Hypercurve full includes ignored tests; four ignored minimal tests are covered in full.
Hypermesh defaults are empty. Both no-default and all-feature suites use --include-ignored with YEAHRIGHT_BENCH=1.
HR/HC fuzz targets compile only. No fresh fuzz campaign, coverage run, or full Hyperlimit/Hyperlattice/Hypertri/Hypersolve standalone suite is claimed.
Concurrent Hyperreal computable drafts are excluded. Full live integration and Hypercurve release readiness remain open.

timings.interpretation: All runs retained, no favorable subrange or unchanged-binary retries. Each variant is a different source revision. Timing matrices meet the prespecified within-binary whole-process max/min <=1.5 guard. Mapped wall times round to zero and support correctness only. Criterion whole-process time includes setup, not just algorithm latency.

profiles.workload: Single complete all-feature libtest process running the 12,100-pair equality oracle, including its independent expected cross-products; equal-length control-test/changed-test names.
profiles.limits: Not geometry-only attribution, ecosystem memory coverage, a leak proof, or latency evidence. Instrumented runs do not overlap timing matrices.

resource_events: Initial sandbox and approved host builds hit the per-user /tmp quota. Both failure logs remain. Builds moved to this evidence root with a task-local TMPDIR.

With approval, only the previous angular checkpoint's completed UI target cache was cleaned (Cargo reported 7,385 files/5.1 GiB). All 440 previous proof artifacts were reverified and preserved. Rebuilds regenerate that cache.
The 1.6 MiB incomplete /tmp build cache could not be cargo-cleaned because its quota-truncated cache tag was invalid. It was moved recoverably to failed-tmp-cache under this root, not deleted.

HR fuzz and the Hyperlattice mimalloc build first failed on sandbox ccache writes. Approved escalated retries succeeded; original failures remain. Read-only binary-size collection also required an approved child-process-permission retry.
limitations: The 22-gate ecosystem result qualifies the rejected guarded candidate, not a shipped runtime change. Retained final-source validation is separately recorded.
No fresh fuzz campaign, coverage run, standalone full Hyperlimit/Hyperlattice/Hypertri/Hypersolve suites, or final live concurrent-draft integration is claimed.
CPU affinity is fixed but desktop activity, scheduling, frequency scaling and thermal conditions are uncontrolled. Small changes are observations, not universal guarantees.
Native .text grows for every measured final-guarded binary; WASM shrinks 2,918 bytes. These mixed size changes do not rescue the higher-priority performance costs.
followups: Use the retained equality guards to investigate a shared magnitude-comparison core or cheaper common exits without imposing the measured close-fraction and geometry costs. Do not add another filter/cache or public compatibility interface.
Remove Hypercurve's single-iteration coarse tensor-box refinement scaffolding while preserving fallthrough to exact-fiber specialization when endpoint ordering is undecided.
Continue non-angular retained point/coordinate policy audits and single-authority CurveRegion2 consolidation; requalify finalized concurrent lower-stack changes.
